title: Shipment Pricing Refactor
flaw: Same carrier-type conditional chain duplicated across three functions (Strategy-shaped gap); primitive obsession on a raw carrier string instead of a literal union; boolean-parameter trap on isExpress/isFragile; magic-number rate literals scattered per branch.

title: Patient Vitals Monitor
flaw: useEffect fetching vitals on patientId change has no guard against out-of-order responses, so a stale fetch for a previously selected patient can resolve after a newer one and silently overwrite the currently displayed patient's vitals - an async race condition that only shows up when requests resolve out of order.
key_learnings: useEffect's cleanup runs right before the effect re-runs for a new dependency value (or on unmount) - it's the hook for marking a previous render's in-flight async work as stale.

AbortController only cancels anything if the signal is actually threaded into the request *and* every implementation (real fetch and test fakes) respects it - calling .abort() on a controller nobody passed the signal to is a no-op.
mistakes: First attempt had no cleanup/guard at all, so a stale response could freely overwrite newer state.
Second attempt added an AbortController but never passed abort.signal into fetchVitals, so .abort() had nothing to cancel - same bug persisted.
review_changes: Walked through a local didCancel flag set in the effect's cleanup and checked in .then()/.catch() before calling setState.

Walked through the full AbortController version: extending FetchVitals to accept a signal, threading it into the real fetch(), special-casing AbortError in .catch(), and updating test fakes to honor the signal.
next_focus: Another exercise in the same stale-closure/out-of-order-async-effect family before advancing categories, so it can be mastered before moving on.

title: Username Availability Field
flaw: Debounced username-availability check has no guard against out-of-order async resolution: the effect keyed on the debounced value calls checkAvailability and sets status/suggestion directly in .then()/.catch() with no comparison against the current debounced value or a request id, so if an earlier keystroke's slower check resolves after a later keystroke's faster one, the stale result silently overwrites the status (and Continue-button enablement) for the username currently in the box - same stale-closure/out-of-order-async-effect race as the prior two exercises, held at the same difficulty and category since the last one (WatchlistQuotePanel) is still unreviewed/assigned and the category hasn't yet landed a 'completed' status since the original 'struggled' entry.

title: Listing Detail Panel
flaw: handleSelect fires fetchListingDetail directly inside the card's onClick handler and sets detail/status straight from its .then()/.catch() with no guard comparing the resolved listing's id (or a request id) against the currently selected listing, so if an earlier click's slower fetch resolves after a later click's faster one, the stale listing's detail silently overwrites the panel while the list still shows the newer listing as selected - same stale-closure/out-of-order-async race family as the prior three exercises, this time triggered from an imperative event-handler fetch rather than a useEffect (no dependency array or cleanup function to lean on), held at the same difficulty and category since the category still hasn't landed a 'completed' status since the original 'struggled' entry on exercise 2.
